question: Does the publicly accessible AABE issue PDF add an independent fish survey or station-resolved evidence for the two Manila esteros?

accessAndPublicationFinding.access: The public 77-page Asian Journal of Biology Education issue PDF was reviewed in place. It contains an AABE23 conference-abstract section and Orozco's abstract on printed page 53; no file or page image was retained.
accessAndPublicationFinding.dateConflict: The issue cover and table of contents identify Volume 6: December 2012. The abstract page footer says Asian Journal of Biology Education Vol. 6 (2010), and the issue editorial identifies the AABE23 conference as held 18–20 October 2010. Preserve these conflicting issue/abstract dates; do not assign a definitive publication year to the abstract without further bibliographic evidence.
accessAndPublicationFinding.authorAndAffiliation: The abstract lists Glorina Orozco as its sole author and Far Eastern University as affiliation.

sourceFindings.reportedPattern: The abstract says Rasbora and Gambusia were dominant across the two esteros. It provides no species-to-estero or species-to-station assignments.
sourceFindings.lineageComparison: The same two waterbodies and four fish labels appear in the related DLSU 2008 article abstract, Springer 2012 chapter abstract, and UPLB 2024 abstract compilation. The matching summaries indicate a related publication lineage, but do not prove that all records come from one identical field dataset or that separate campaigns occurred.
sourceFindings.documentTypeLimit: The retrieved item is a conference abstract within the journal issue, not the full 2008 article, thesis, 2012 chapter, or an underlying sampling dataset. It adds no methods, field dates, station list, species-by-station table, voucher IDs, coordinates, or independent sample evidence.

rightsReview.finding: The issue displays a general copyright notice, © 2004 Asian Association for Biology Education, all rights reserved. No item-specific open reuse license or permission was identified.
rightsReview.handling: No PDF, abstract text, page image, table, figure, or raw record was copied or retained; only short attributed research findings are summarized.

evidenceDecision.decision: Add the proceedings abstract as a public-source lineage reference only; treat it with the existing Orozco/Zafaralla two-estero research lineage and do not count it as an additional independent survey.

nonClaims: The conference abstract is not evidence of four additional species records or an independent survey relative to the 2008 and 2012 related abstracts.
The abstract does not assign any named fish to Estero de San Miguel versus Estero de Quiapo or to a particular station.
The named esteros are not interchangeable with Pasig River fish localities; this source does not establish a Pasig River occurrence.
The issue date mismatch does not establish which year the abstract was first published or whether the 2012 book chapter reuses the same underlying samples.
nextActions: If an authorized complete article, thesis, or chapter becomes available, compare its sampling dates, stations, methods, fish table, and vouchers with the conference abstract before resolving dataset overlap.

Continue searching for NCR freshwater and estuary sources with explicit waterbody, taxon, and sample provenance, while keeping shared-water and historical abstract leads separate from occurrence assertions.
